sentences.text: Piscivorenantiornis was a small bird belonging to the Enantiornithes group, a diverse lineage of early avians.
Its skull preserves a pair of craniolateral processes that are absent in most other enantiornithines.
The pubic boot is large with a tip that is strongly recurved.
The genus name means "fish-eater" in Latin, marking it as the first known piscivorous enantiornithine.
Fossil evidence suggests the bird swallowed fish bones that were later regurgitated as a gastric pellet shortly before death.
The holotype specimen was discovered near Dapingfang in Chaoyang County, Liaoning, China, within the Jiufotang Formation.
A second specimen of the species was described in 2020.
In its original description, the genus nested either alongside Pterygornis or outside a clade containing Pterygornis and Dunhuangia.
A later study recovered the genus outside of a clade comprising Mirusavis and Shangyang.
The fossil range is the Early Cretaceous (Aptian stage).
The animal lived between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago during the Aptian stage.
